cell_notes.h-lists-resources-at-startup: changed from y at 0.99.1. Since 1.2.0 Pi no longer lists resources when a server connects: /mcp and `pi mcp list` show that a server offers resources instead of counting them (CHANGELOG 1.2.0, https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10526). Resources are still reachable through the resource tools (h-reads-resource).
cell_notes.h-startup-timeout: level 1 held the stub's reply 10 s, which matches Pi's documented first-prompt wait ("waits up to 10 seconds", docs/mcp.md "Startup" in the package). Since 0.99.2 that wait covers only servers with `direct` tools; codemode servers connect in the background (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212). With the stub answering at once the turn ended about 1 s in, before any server had answered initialize; at 5 s it ended before util, held 8 s, answered. So Pi no longer blocks the first prompt on a slow codemode server, and lists it once it connects.
cell_notes.h-reads-resource: the Pi resource script in plan/harness_sessions.yaml names the server first (`await describeNamespace('mcp__def')`) before calling `tools.read_mcp_resource`, exactly as docs/mcp.md "Startup" describes: "a codemode script waits for the servers it names (`mcp__<server>`)". Pi's script only. Since 1.2.0 the resource tools are registered only once a server with resources has connected, and the call 0.1 s into the turn without that line fails with "tools.read_mcp_resource does not exist" (0/3 at 1.2.0 with the 0.99.1 script).

cell_notes.h-tools-offered-to-model: measured headless in default approval mode. Non-interactive Gemini CLI withholds any tool that would ask, so no MCP tool reaches the model (https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/policy-engine); with --approval-mode yolo all 46 that reached the registry are offered, which is every fixture tool but util's unfetched pages (level2-*-read_only-unattended-*/model.jsonl). Interactive mode asks instead of withholding, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-destructive-blocked-by-default: measured headless in default approval mode, where the tool is withheld from the model rather than held at a prompt (https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/policy-engine). Interactive mode prompts, which this run does not measure.
cell_notes.h-read-only-runs-without-prompt: measured headless in default approval mode, where search_records is withheld from the model despite readOnlyHint (https://geminicli.com/docs/reference/policy-engine). Interactive mode prompts, which this run does not measure.

notes: Every cell's evidence is the capture path and the message ids, so a maintainer can open the JSONL and see exactly what their harness sent.

h-negotiated-revision.title: Negotiated revision
h-negotiated-revision.question: Which protocol revision does the agent request, and which does it settle on?
h-negotiated-revision.description: When an agent connects, it asks for an MCP revision and the server answers with the one they will use. We record both, over stdio and over HTTP, against a test server on MCP 2025-11-25 and one on 2026-07-28.
h-negotiated-revision.observe: initialize request params.protocolVersion and the response, on the stdio and the HTTP session. Cell is the revision string, not y/a/n; it names each transport when they differ.

h-tool-count-limit.title: Tool count limit
h-tool-count-limit.question: How many tools will it take from one server?
h-tool-count-limit.description: We can't see how many tools an agent keeps, so the cell records how many pages of the 150-tool server it fetched and whether it stopped early. Caps an agent documents, such as VS Code's 128, appear as notes.
h-tool-count-limit.observe: the number of tools the harness later exposes cannot be seen; instead the fixture logs whether the harness stops paging early or disconnects. Cell is the page count reached plus any documented cap (VS Code 128, Cascade 100) as a note.

h-reacts-to-list-changed.title: Reacts to list changed
h-reacts-to-list-changed.question: When a server says its tool list changed, does it fetch the list again?

h-answers-ping.question: When a server pings it, does it answer within 5 seconds?
h-answers-ping.description: After connecting, the server pings the agent, once over stdio and once over HTTP. Yes if the agent replies within 5 seconds on both, some if on only one. MCP 2026-07-28 removed ping, so an agent that settles on 2026-07-28 has nothing to answer and shows as not measured there.
h-answers-ping.observe: the recorder sends a server-initiated ping after the handshake, on the stdio and the HTTP session; a response within 5s. y / n per transport, a when the transports differ.

h-startup-timeout.title: Startup timeout
h-startup-timeout.question: How long does it wait for a slow server before giving up?
h-startup-timeout.description: One test server waits 8 seconds before answering the agent's first request. Yes if the agent waits and keeps the server, no if it drops it. The note gives how long the agent actually waited.
h-startup-timeout.observe: util delays initialize by 8s; cell is whether util was still listed (y) or dropped (n), with the observed wait as a note.

notes_by_num.2: 2025-11-25 fixture: level1-2025-11-25-slow-start/util.jsonl seq 6 tools/list; util answered its first request after 8.2s; 2026-07-28 fixture: level1-2026-07-28-slow-start/util.jsonl seq 6 tools/list; util answered its first request after 8.3s; fresh.json: all four freshness checks (home, servers_listed, tools_offered, egress) passed in 72/72 sessions; level 1: the stub held its reply 10 s (LEVEL1_REPLY_DELAY_S in scripts/harnesses/pi_cli.py), so the turn outlasted the background connect; context: level 1 held the stub's reply 10 s, which matches Pi's documented first-prompt wait ("waits up to 10 seconds", docs/mcp.md "Startup" in the package). Since 0.99.2 that wait covers only servers with `direct` tools; codemode servers connect in the background (https://github.com/earendil-works/pi/issues/10212). h-tools-offered-to-model.title: Tools offered to model
h-tools-offered-to-model.question: Which of a server's tools does the agent offer its model, and do their descriptions, schemas and annotations arrive unchanged?
h-tools-offered-to-model.description: A scripted stand-in for the model records the agent's first request to it. We compare each tool in that request with what the servers listed: whether it was offered, whether its description and input schema arrived unchanged, and whether hints such as destructiveHint reached the model at all. Yes if every tool arrived unchanged, some if any are missing or changed, no if none were offered.
h-tools-offered-to-model.observe: the first model request the stub receives in the level-1 stdio session, against every tool the fixtures answered in tools/list. Per tool, whether it was offered, whether its description and input schema arrived unchanged, and whether its annotations reached the model as a field or as hint names anywhere in the request. y all offered unchanged, a some missing or changed, n none offered. Cell value summarises the counts.

h-destructive-blocked-by-default.title: Destructive blocked by default
h-destructive-blocked-by-default.question: In default approval mode, is the destructive call held for confirmation?
h-destructive-blocked-by-default.description: In the agent's default mode, we ask it to use a tool marked destructive, three times. The tool deletes nothing; only its name and hints are under test. Yes if the agent holds the call for confirmation every time. Ran without asking if the call reached the server. Not measured if the agent has no machine-readable output and the call never arrived, because then held and never tried look the same.
h-destructive-blocked-by-default.observe: no tools/call delete_account reaches the server AND the harness output (stream-json/NDJSON) contains a permission request event. y if held in 3/3, n if the call reached the server, a mixed. u if the harness has no machine-readable output and the call did not arrive, since "held" and "never tried" cannot be told apart.

h-read-only-runs-without-prompt.question: In default mode, does a readOnlyHint tool run without a confirmation?
h-read-only-runs-without-prompt.description: In the agent's default mode, we ask it to use a tool marked read-only, three times. Yes if the call runs without a confirmation prompt. Few agents document doing this: Claude Desktop, VS Code Copilot, ChatGPT, Codex in writes mode and Qwen Code in auto mode.
h-read-only-runs-without-prompt.observe: tools/call search_records arrives with no permission event preceding it. This is the annotation-honoring cell; documented only for Claude Desktop, VS Code Copilot, ChatGPT, Codex writes mode, Qwen auto mode.

h-answers-elicitation.title: Answers elicitation
h-answers-elicitation.question: When a tool asks the user for input mid-call (elicitation), does the agent answer?
h-answers-elicitation.description: A test tool asks the user for input in the middle of the call (MCP elicitation). On MCP 2025-11-25 the server sends a separate request, and the agent passes if it replies with accept, decline or cancel instead of an error. On 2026-07-28 the tool asks through its result, and the agent passes if it calls the tool again with an answer. We test whichever revision the agent negotiates.
h-answers-elicitation.observe: the cf tool's elicitation/create request receives a response (accept/decline/cancel) rather than an error. Deprecated-status note on 2026-07-28; MRTR measured instead where the harness negotiates 2026.

h-answers-sampling.title: Answers sampling
h-answers-sampling.question: When a tool asks the agent's model for a completion mid-call (sampling), does the agent answer?
h-answers-sampling.description: A test tool asks the agent's model to write something in the middle of the call (MCP sampling). On MCP 2025-11-25 the server sends a separate request, and the agent passes if it replies with a completion instead of an error. On 2026-07-28 the tool asks through its result, and the agent passes if it calls the tool again with a completion. We test whichever revision the agent negotiates. Sampling is deprecated as of 2026-07-28: it still works, but new implementations should call a model provider's API directly, and it may be removed no earlier than 2027-07-28.
h-answers-sampling.observe: sampling/createMessage from cf receives a completion rather than an error. Where the harness negotiates 2026-07-28, the MRTR form instead, as for elicitation - the tools/call result carries an inputRequests sampling/createMessage and y is a retry of the call with inputResponses.

h-tolerates-progress.title: Tolerates progress
h-tolerates-progress.question: Does it wait out a slow tool that sends progress updates, without cancelling it?
h-tolerates-progress.description: We ask the agent to run a slow tool that sends progress updates as it works. Yes if it waits for the tool to finish, some if it cancels after updates arrive, no if it fails before any arrive.
h-tolerates-progress.observe: the slow session completes with progress notifications received and no cancellation. y completes, a cancels after progress, n fails before.
